The glob re-export keeps every pub item available at its drain:: path.

summary: The move itself is clean. It shifts the pid-file, stop, restart and RealLifecycle section, unchanged, from drain.rs into a new drain/lifecycle.rs. It re-exports that code with `pub use lifecycle::*`, widens two test-used helpers to pub(super), and adds a CHANGELOG entry. The workspace builds, and the recorded fmt, clippy and test runs passed. But it does not achieve the goal the request and criterion 1 set. I counted drain.rs's production lines the way code_health::measure_source counts them (total lines minus the #[cfg(test)] module ranges). The new drain.rs has 6522 lines, and its five test modules fill lines 4010–4064, 4066–5125, 5127–5232, 5234–6197 and 6199–6522, which leaves about 4013 production lines (my count from reading those line positions). That is far over the 1500 busy limit, and over the 2000 absolute limit too. Before the change it was about 4588. The "1798" in the request was measured when the request was queued on 2026-10-26, and the file has grown a lot since then. The producer moved one 578-line block and never re-measured. The reading's own fallback was to move more cohesive groups until drain.rs is under 1500, and it was not followed. So drain.rs stays over its limits, and code health will raise the same structural pass again.
